# Review, pass 1 (units) — iliad-159 (24.707–804)

Checked: every grammatical label in every note against the line; `t` against the packet (identical, all 98 lines, no line missing or doubled); `ln` of every unit; quotation marks and `mark` (“ on 716, 725, 748, 762, 778; ” on 717, 745, 759, 775, 781; all speech openings and closings match); `l` against `t`; `l` ↔ `i`; table conformity (Iliad table, then the Odyssey table); repeated lines (741, 746, 788, 790, 791 agree with the published English). Neighbouring part: iliad-158 ends with Cassandra’s speech closed (”), so 707 correctly opens without a mark. `t` was not touched.

## Line 769 (flagged by the scanner), scanned by hand
δαέρων ἢ γαλόων ἢ εἰνατέρων εὐπέπλων has 15 syllables. At 762 δαέρων scans δα⏑ ε⏑ ρων– (a dactyl’s two shorts). At line-start 769 it cannot do that: it scans only if δαέ- is run together into one long syllable, or δα- is long and the final -ρων is shortened before ἢ. Then ἢ γα λο | ων ἢ | εἰ να τε | ρων εὐ | πε πλων: a spondaic fifth foot, and ἢ left long in hiatus before εἰνατέρων. The irregularity is real. The drafter’s sentence was right in outline but incomplete (it gave only the synizesis option and said δα- "has to be counted long", which alone does not scan); rewritten as one sentence (see change 10).

## Findings considered and refused
- 768–770 `l` "a father, so kind always" vs `i` "as kind as a father": ὣς is printed with the accent of the demonstrative; `l` keeps it literally and the note explains the sense. Left.
- 773 `i` "grieving in heart" (table has "at heart" at 23.284 but "in heart" at 7.428 for ἀχνύμενος κῆρ): the table is itself split; the shipped 7.428 wording is followed. Left.
- 784 ἄσπετον ὕλην "boundless wood" vs the table's ἄσπετον ὕλην "boundless forest" (2.455): here the logs for the pyre are meant and the note says "wood". Left, but the drafter should add the departure to new-renderings.md (not edited by the reviewer).
- 757–759 οἷς (possessive "his own") not glossed: the Odyssey table's wording "his gentle shafts" is followed, and the note already marks the stock phrase. Left.
- 726/730 νήπιος "infant" vs "little children" for νήπια τέκνα: matches the table (`l` "infant children", `i` "little children"). Left.
- 725 ἆνερ "Husband", 709 ἄγοντι, 713 κε + imperfect, 716–717 ἄσεσθε (future sense read, aorist subjunctive also possible; the note says "read here with future sense"): labels true. Left.
- ἀμιχθαλόεσσαν "misty", ἀσύφηλον "disgraceful", ἀτρυγέτοιο: unknown meaning is said; follows the table. Left.

# Review, pass 2 (gloss.json) — iliad-159

Checked all 86 novel-form entries and the four `__broaden__` entries against the Greek and the units’ `l`/`i`; entry rules (under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no line numbers, no "here") verified by script. `units.json` needed no change in pass 2; `t` untouched.

## Changes
| # | Entry | Severity | What was wrong | What done |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | δαέρων | moderate | "with πάντων after a superlative: ’of all’" mislabels the parse: πάντων is a separate word agreeing with δαέρων; δαέρων is the partitive genitive after φίλτατε, and elsewhere stands in a list of relatives | rewritten: partitive after a superlative, or in a list of relatives |
| 2 | πεφρίκασιν | moderate | rendering ’shudder at’ contradicts the unit (`l` "bristle at", `i` "bristle with fear at") and the table (shudder is ῥιγέω) | ’bristle with fear at, shrink from’ |

| 4 | ἐφορμηθεῖεν | minor | "rush upon, attack": the table turns down "attack" | "rush upon" only |
| 5 | πρόσφατος | minor | "freshly killed" imports the context into the lexical meaning (new-renderings: πρόσφατος alone is "fresh") | "fresh, new" |

## Findings considered and refused
- οὐρεῦσι "mule", dat. pl. of οὐρεύς (nom. pl. οὐρῆες): correct, and the unit’s dative with εἴξατε is right. Left.
- παραιφάμενος, aor. part. mid. of παράφημι, "talk over, coax": agrees with `l` "talking-round" and `i` "coax him round". Left.
- ῥύσκευ (ῥύ-σκε-ο > -ευ, iterative impf. 2 sg. mid.): correct. Left.
- ἀμφίσταθ’ = ἀμφίστατο, τ > θ before the rough breathing of ὅμιλος: parse and note agree. Left.
- `__broaden__` λόχον, πρῶται, δαῖτα: old entries whole, new readings true of the lines. Left.
- 771 `i` "would coax … hold back" for the imperfects: habitual sense, matches the note (‘you used to hold him back’). Left.
- 757 ἐποιχόμενος `l` "assailing" vs `i` "came upon": the note says ‘coming upon’; both within the sense of the verb. Left.
